prediction_scored: not scored. The registration made the test conditional on a first stage: FHV and taxi pickups inside the area had to fall relative to outside, with an interval excluding zero. More than 10% of FHV trips had no pickup zone in three of the four windows (19.3% and 18.3% in 2018, 10.9% in January 2019), so by the registered rule the gate used taxis alone, and taxi pickups changed by +1.82% (-0.85 to +4.57). The combined series gives -1.06% (-2.35 to +0.26) and FHV alone -1.86% (-3.39 to -0.31). The gate failed, so the verdict is no_test. The registered subway estimate is -0.71% (-2.02 to +0.62), with a placebo of -0.45% (-1.14 to +0.23); had the gate passed, the verdict would have been unsettled.
settle: Two things. First, a first stage that measures the treatment: the surcharge applies to any trip that touches the area, so a trip from an airport to Midtown is charged although its pickup is outside. Trips touching the area need a comparison that is not charged, for example trips of similar length wholly outside it, from records with complete zones (the high-volume files from February 2019 are complete; the 2018 FHV files are not). Second, a subway measure that can see an effect of a few tenths of a percent: entries by hour and fare type at stations nearest the places where short for-hire trips fell most, or the MTA origin-destination estimates, which begin only in 2021 and so cover the 2025 toll but not the 2019 surcharge.

notes: Subway, 2019 (registered): 77 complexes inside and 331 outside, 156 grid cells; mean weekday entries in the 2019 pre window 2,478,997 inside and 2,652,729 outside. Sensitivities: control Manhattan north of 96th St -0.92% (-2.57 to +0.76); control Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens -0.67% (-2.15 to +0.83); unweighted +0.17% (-0.80 to +1.15); with the 96 St complexes -0.69% (-2.00 to +0.63); without L complexes -0.90% (-2.29 to +0.52); 16-week post window -0.99% (-2.40 to +0.43); nights 20:00-04:00 +2.17% (-0.42 to +4.83) with a night placebo of -1.11% (-3.40 to +1.23); weekends +1.07% (-16.90 to +22.92); 2019 alone -0.85% (-2.43 to +0.76). The standard error is 0.679 log points x 100, so the smallest effect the test could detect with 80% power is about 1.92%, above the +1.3% registered as the largest plausible effect. The registered composed range could not be computed as planned because the gate series did not fall. Exploratory, not registered: FHV and taxi trips touching the area were 590,902 a weekday before and 569,645 after, against 565,502 and 569,898 in the same weeks of 2018, a change of -4.34% with no comparison area (about 25,651 trips a weekday). With the registered constants this would add 0.174% to zone entries (range 0.026% to 0.776%), which the subway test cannot distinguish from zero. Li and Vignon (2024) report larger falls (11% ride-hail, 8% taxi). Secondary, 2025 zone toll (descriptive): entries at CBD complexes against all others, January-March 2025 against autumn 2024, less the same a year earlier, -1.23% (-2.75 to +0.33); placebo +1.44% (-0.24 to +3.16); against Manhattan north of 60th St -0.24% (-1.85 to +1.40); nights -0.60% (-2.97 to +1.82). Entries are counted where riders board, so a commuter who leaves a car at home adds an entry outside the zone in the morning and one inside in the evening. One week of 2019 ridership (13-19 May, used only by the 16-week sensitivity) timed out as a weekly query and was fetched day by day. Two-week queries cached before the chunk size was changed are not used.
